source.title: A Theory of Usable Information Under Computational Constraints

confidence_rationale: Predictive V-information measures information relative to a restricted family V of decoders an observer can use. Unlike Shannon mutual information it can be created by computation, breaking the data processing inequality. This formalises GOV-CONTRACT-3's key clause: 'the information exists somewhere' (Shannon) is not 'the receiver can use it' (V-information). Held at 0.6 because V is set by the modeller and the paper gives no guidance on choosing V for a biological or REE receiver, and it models decoder class but not latency or robustness.
failure_signatures: The choice of decoder family V decides the answer; a governance user could pick V to make a desired reduction pass or fail.
V-information covers decoder power but not the rule's other cost terms (side-channel complexity, latency, robustness), so it grounds one clause, not the whole cost function.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Shannon mutual information ignores the observer's computational limits; predictive V-information, defined relative to a family V of predictive models, includes mutual information as a special case, can be increased by computation (violating the data processing inequality), and can be estimated reliably with PAC-style guarantees.
mapping.ree_translation: GOV-CONTRACT-3 distinguishes information-theoretic reducibility (inadmissible) from computational/operational reducibility (admissible). V-information is the published formal version of that split: a candidate is reducible for receiver B if its V_B-information is recoverable from the smaller basis, where V_B is B's decoder class. For ARC-144, 'what B cannot cheaply reconstruct' is naturally the gap between Shannon and V_B-information.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper is about predictors on datasets, not modules in an agent; V is a hypothesis class, not a compute or latency budget. It supports the rule's standard as a coherent, formalisable notion; it does not validate the three collapse requirements or the relocation checklist.
mapping.source_context: ML theory paper proposing V-information and showing its uses in structure learning and fair representation learning.

confidence_components.notes: Strongest formal support found for GOV-CONTRACT-3's operational standard. Metadata from WebSearch hits (ICLR 2020, arXiv 2002.10689); pages egress-blocked, no DOI.
